written: 2026-11-19, while six teacher subagents were writing the variants and before any SeedLM-5 coder was trained or any variant was checked
motivation: Three coders each fix 4 of the 29 held-out development tasks the engine fails (s3-pyx, s3b-pyx, s4-post), although s4-post doubled the in-distribution rate (held-out teacher tasks, first beam program reproduces the example: 23.7% -> 47.5%). The teacher tasks were imagined by category; the tasks the engine fails are a region of their own (its blind spots), and the coder had seen only 82 real programs from it (development one-liners, training part)
hypothesis: Teacher-written neighbours of the training pool's engine failures teach the coder that region, so a coder trained with them fixes more held-out engine failures than s4-post with the same architecture and compute
data: seeds: the 91 training-pool tasks (MBPP train split and the extra pool's training part) without a known correct library program (scripts/seedlm5_seeds.py); per seed a teacher writes 2 restatements and 6 neighbours, each a one-line pyx-writable task with three inputs (data/seedlm/variant_tasks_part*.json), checked by scripts/seedlm3_task_check.py and decontaminated against every evaluation description by scripts/seedlm3_decontaminate.py --prefix variant_tasks. The variants of a tenth of the seeds (by a hash of the seed id) are held out
coder: s5-var: scripts/seedlm4_train.py --name s5-var --minutes 120 --variant-share 0.1, everything else as s4-post (the share is taken from the synthetic rows)
primary_measure: on the extra pool's held-out fifth (94 tasks), the number of tasks the engine fails that pyx_model solves (s3-pyx, s3b-pyx and s4-post: 4 each). Supported if at least 7 (three more than every earlier coder); 5 or 6 is inconclusive; 4 or fewer is not supported
secondary_measures: held-out failing development tasks with a teacher one-liner (15): the first verified program passes the task's tests (s4-post 3)
variants of held-out seeds: first beam program reproduces the visible example (no earlier coder was measured on them)
held-out teacher tasks: first beam program reproduces the example (s4-post 47.5%), to see whether the generic tasks suffer
methods: the eight methods of SeedLM-3, computed by scripts/seedlm4_tasks.py
choice: s5-var replaces s3-pyx only if its best method solves more held-out tasks than s3-pyx's 68 (ties keep s3-pyx); ties among methods in SeedLM-3's order
then: a chosen s5-var gets the same validation gate (alone no fewer than the engine's 19 of 45; in the 1.5B pipeline no fewer than 31), one MBPP+ test run and one HumanEval+ run
caveat: a gain could come from more teacher data of any kind rather than from its region; doubling the generic teacher tasks (s3-pyx -> s3b-pyx) did not change the primary measure, which is the nearest control available

addendum_1.written: 2026-11-19, after s4-post's discovery diagnostic and before the variants were checked or any SeedLM-5 coder trained
addendum_1.reason: on the 15 held-out engine failures with a teacher one-liner, s4-post's oracle is close to its first verified program (4 vs 3 at width 32) and the teacher's program sits a median 36.3 nats below the beam's best (quartiles 17.6 / 36.3 / 99.5): the coder does not propose those programs at all. A continuous measure of that gap has more power than a count out of 15
addendum_1.secondary_measure: scripts/seedlm3_discovery.py --model s5-var --widths 8 32 128 on the same sets; the hypothesis predicts the teacher programs move closer to the beam's best on the 15 engine failures: a lower median gap than s4-post's 36.3 nats, with the gap shrinking on at least 10 of the 15 tasks (paired by task, counts only)

outcome.primary: 5 of 29 engine failures solved by pyx_model (s3-pyx, s3b-pyx, s4-post: 4 each): inconclusive by the pre-registered rule; all 5 are among the 6 tasks the earlier coders reached (reports/seedlm/overlap_holdout_s5.json)

secondary.teacher_holdout_top1_reproduces: 48.2% (s4-post 47.5%): the generic tasks did not suffer

outcome.addendum_1: beyond gold gap median 36.3 -> 29.4 nats, shrinking on 9 of 15 tasks (4 grow, 2 zero in both): the median criterion holds, the 10-of-15 criterion does not
outcome.validation_gate: passed with ties: 19 alone (engine 19), 31 in the 1.5B pipeline (stored 31)
outcome.test: pyx_override 72 alone (engine 68; s3-pyx's pyx_tie_fill 68); 98 in the 1.5B pipeline (98); 82 in the 0.5B pipeline (80)
outcome.diagnostics: training programs as they are cover 4 of 29 engine failures (reports/seedlm/coverage_holdout.json); the coder finds 29 of 37 held-out teacher programs it has seen whole but 17 of 77 with a new link or twig (reports/seedlm/fragments_s5-var.json); see docs/seed_lm5.md
